key_insight: 3D Cartesian PDE operators can be treated as repeated 1D line solves along each axis, eliminating the need to assemble or store full 3D matrices.
engineering_relevance: This enables matrix-free CFD solvers with O(N) work and low memory footprint, making high-order and production-scale Cartesian simulations more hardware-efficient.
method: Kronecker-product factorization reduces 3D operators to tensor-product 1D kernels
Multi-right-hand-side reshaping turns sweeps into batched line solves; dense cases map to GEMM, sparse cases to banded/stencil kernels
Sum factorization and pencil decomposition improve high-order Galerkin throughput and parallel scalability
evidence_signal: The abstract synthesizes known CFD and numerical PDE techniques and analyzes their cost structure, reporting O(N) compute scaling and O(Nx+Ny+Nz) operator storage up to bandwidth constants.
watch_item: Performance depends on maintaining axis-contiguous data layouts and efficient line-solve implementations, especially for nonuniform stencils or MPI pencil decompositions.
paper_title: No 3D Matrices: A Unified Tensor-Product View of Matrix-Free Cartesian PDE Solvers
